hints: Recall that distance on a velocity-time graph is the area under the graph.
Calculate the area of the triangular region for the first 8 seconds: $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 12.6$.
walkthrough:
Calculate distance as the area of the triangular region from $t = 0$ to $t = 8$:
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2}(8)(12.6) = 4 \times 12.6 = 50.4\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Name the foundational principle: the distance covered is equal to the area under the velocity-time graph.
Over the first $8\text{ s}$, the graph forms a right triangle with base $8\text{ s}$ and height $12.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Express the speed at $t = 62\text{ s}$ using the first deceleration phase: $v_{62} = 12.6 - 14a$.
Express the speed at $t = 62\text{ s}$ using the final deceleration to rest: $0 = v_{62} - 2a(8) \implies v_{62} = 16a$.
walkthrough:
Express the velocity at $t = 62\text{ s}$ using the first deceleration stage ($48 \leq t \leq 62$, $\Delta t = 14\text{ s}$):
$$v_{62} = 12.6 - a(62 - 48) = 12.6 - 14a$$

Express the velocity at $t = 62\text{ s}$ using the final deceleration stage to rest ($62 \leq t \leq 70$, $\Delta t = 8\text{ s}$):
$$0 = v_{62} - 2a(70 - 62) \implies v_{62} = 16a$$

Equate the two expressions and solve for $a$:
$$12.6 - 14a = 16a$$
$$30a = 12.6 \implies a = \frac{12.6}{30} = 0.42\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Apply the constant acceleration relation $v = u + at$ to the first deceleration phase from $t = 48\text{ s}$ to $t = 62\text{ s}$ with deceleration $a$:
$$\Delta t_1 = 62 - 48 = 14\text{ s}$$
$$v_{62} = 12.6 - 14a\quad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

Apply the constant acceleration relation to the second deceleration phase from $t = 62\text{ s}$ to $t = 70\text{ s}$ with deceleration $2a$, noting that the bus comes to rest ($v_{70} = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$):
$$\Delta t_2 = 70 - 62 = 8\text{ s}$$
$$0 = v_{62} - (2a)(8)$$
$$v_{62} = 16a\quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

Divide both sides by 30:
$$a = \frac{12.6}{30} = 0.42\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

hints: Calculate the intermediate speed at $t = 62\text{ s}$: $v_{62} = 16(0.42) = 6.72\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Calculate the distance for each of the four journey segments: $s_1 = 50.4\text{ m}$, $s_2 = 40 \times 12.6 = 504\text{ m}$, $s_3 = \frac{1}{2}(12.6 + 6.72)(14) = 135.24\text{ m}$, and $s_4 = \frac{1}{2}(8)(6.72) = 26.88\text{ m}$.
Sum the segment distances to find the total distance $s_{\text{total}} = 716.52\text{ m}$.
Divide total distance by the total duration $70\text{ s}$ to determine the average speed.
walkthrough:
Find the speed of the bus at $t = 62\text{ s}$:
$$v_{62} = 16a = 16(0.42) = 6.72\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Sum the distances to find the total distance:
$$s_{\text{total}} = 50.4 + 504 + 135.24 + 26.88 = 716.52\text{ m}$$

Compute the average speed over the total time of $70\text{ s}$:
$$\text{Average speed} = \frac{s_{\text{total}}}{\text{Total time}} = \frac{716.52}{70} = 10.236\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
First, compute the speed of the bus at $t = 62\text{ s}$:
$$v_{62} = 16a = 16(0.42) = 6.72\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Calculate the area under the velocity-time graph for each of the remaining three sections:

Section 2 ($8 \leq t \leq 48$): rectangle of width $48 - 8 = 40\text{ s}$ and height $12.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s_2 = 40 \times 12.6 = 504\text{ m}$$

Section 3 ($48 \leq t \leq 62$): trapezium with parallel heights $12.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $6.72\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and width $14\text{ s}$:
$$s_3 = \frac{12.6 + 6.72}{2} \times 14 = 19.32 \times 7 = 135.24\text{ m}$$

Section 4 ($62 \leq t \leq 70$): triangle of base $70 - 62 = 8\text{ s}$ and height $6.72\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s_4 = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 6.72 = 4 \times 6.72 = 26.88\text{ m}$$

Add all four segment distances to obtain the total distance:
$$s_{\text{total}} = 50.4 + 504 + 135.24 + 26.88 = 716.52\text{ m}$$

State the formula for average speed and divide by the total elapsed time of $70\text{ s}$:
$$\text{Average speed} = \frac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Total time}} = \frac{716.52}{70} = 10.236\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
